definition: A system of parts working together in a machine; or a way of doing something.
example: The car's steering mechanism felt loose, making it difficult to control.

definition: A person's general attitude towards life or the world; or a probable future situation.
example: She always has a positive outlook on life, even when things are difficult.

definition: The act of moving people or things from one place to another.
example: Many international flights have transit passengers who are just changing planes.

definition: To fail to notice or consider something; or to have a view from above.
example: Our hotel room was perfect because it had a balcony to overlook the sea.

definition: "Hopeless" means feeling that a situation cannot improve, while "Hopeful" means feeling or showing optimism about the future.
example: He was torn between being hopeless about finding a job and remaining hopeful that an opportunity would appear.

definition: To arrange documents or information in a particular order, usually for storage.
example: We need to alphabetically file all these customer records before the end of the day.

definition: To find the origin or cause of something, or to follow a path.
example: Researchers tried to trace the disease back to its initial source.

definition: To put something down carefully in a flat position; for birds, to produce eggs.
example: The chicken is about to lay eggs in the coop.

definition: A series of planned activities to achieve a particular social, commercial, or political goal.
example: The charity plans to launch a new campaign to raise money for clean water.

definition: A curved piece of metal or plastic for hanging things, or something that catches attention.
example: After watching the first episode, I immediately got hooked on the new TV series.

definition: The complete loss or absence of hope.
example: Faced with so many problems, she began to feel deep despair.

definition: For this reason; therefore.
example: The road was wet; hence, driving carefully was essential.

definition: To increase greatly in number or amount; in mathematics, to perform multiplication.
example: If we don't control the rabbits, they will multiply rapidly.

definition: A small round mark; a particular place or position. (Verb: to see or notice)
example: Can you spot the difference between these two pictures?

definition: A general rule, principle, or instruction that helps you decide how to do something.
example: The university provided clear guidelines for writing academic essays.

definition: (For a volcano) to suddenly throw out hot rock, ash, and steam; to burst out.
example: Scientists are monitoring the mountain because a volcano erupts usually after a series of small earthquakes.

definition: To cause someone to come towards something or to notice something.
example: The bright colors of the painting helped draw attention to the exhibition.

definition: To bring a feeling, a memory, or an image into your mind.
example: The old songs always evoke memories of my childhood.

definition: Features belonging to the culture of a particular society, such as traditions, languages, or buildings, that have existed for a long time and have a historical importance.
example: It is important to preserve cultural heritage for future generations.

definition: Happening all the time or very often; remaining the same over time.
example: The temperature inside the lab must remain constant for accurate results.

definition: The part of your body between your waist and the top of your legs, on either side.
example: She hurt her hip when she fell off her bike.

definition: A feeling of surprise and admiration caused by something beautiful, remarkable, or unfamiliar; (verb) to want to know something.
example: I often wonder how birds manage to navigate such long distances.

definition: To behave towards someone or something in a particular way; to give medical care.
example: It's important to treat all students with respect, regardless of their background.

definition: Not usually talking about or drawing attention to your own abilities or achievements; not large or fancy.
example: Even after winning the award, he continued to show modesty and thanked his team.

definition: To encourage the development or growth of ideas or feelings; to care for a child who is not your biological child.
example: The couple decided to foster a child who needed a temporary home.

definition: A person who delivers a message.
example: Please don't shoot the messenger; I'm just telling you what the manager said.

definition: An event or occurrence, especially one that is unusual, important, or violent.
example: There was a major incident on the highway this morning, causing long delays.

definition: Having control or responsibility for something or someone.
example: Who will be in charge of the project while the manager is on vacation?

definition: A strong feeling for or against one group of people or one idea, often without fair judgment.
example: The report was criticized for having a clear political bias.

definition: A very small piece of a hard substance; the seeds of plants like wheat or rice.
example: The farmer planted a new type of grain this season.

definition: A person who is admired for their courage, outstanding achievements, or noble qualities.
example: Firefighters are often seen as brave heroes for their selfless actions.

definition: Lasting only for a short time; short and concise.
example: We had a brief meeting to discuss the main points.

definition: To take hold of something quickly, suddenly, or roughly.
example: I had to try to grab my bag before it fell off the table.

definition: To make someone want to do something, especially something they know they should not do.
example: The delicious smell of the cake was enough to tempt her into eating another slice.

definition: An arm or leg of a person or animal; a large branch of a tree.
example: After the accident, he had an injured limb and couldn't walk easily.

definition: A person, group, or organization competing with others for the same objective or for superiority.
example: Our company faces tough competition from a new rival firm.

definition: The process or industry of getting coal or other minerals from the ground.
example: Many people in the region work in the coal mine.

definition: To speak to; to deal with or discuss a problem or issue.
example: The government needs to address the issue of poverty in the country.

definition: To look at something closely, especially to check its quality or condition.
example: The customs officers will thoroughly inspect all luggage.

definition: To divide into two or more parts; to share something.
example: Let's split the bill equally among us after dinner.

definition: A separate section of a train for passengers; a vehicle pulled by horses.
example: We boarded the last train carriage to find our seats.

definition: A circular ornamental headdress worn by a monarch as a symbol of authority.
example: The queen wore a beautiful diamond crown during the ceremony.

definition: To frighten someone or something.
example: The sudden loud noise scared the living daylights out of me.

definition: Having an affection or liking for someone or something.
example: My grandmother used to be very fond of gardening.

definition: To annoy or cause trouble for someone. "Bothersome" means causing annoyance or trouble.
example: Please don't bother me when I'm studying; your constant interruptions are bothersome.

definition: To say or do something to remove the doubts or fears of someone.
example: She tried to reassure her friend that everything would be okay.

definition: A place providing protection from bad weather or danger; a temporary home.
example: We adopted our dog from the local animal shelter.

definition: A line on the surface of something along which it has split without breaking into separate parts; (verb) to break without separating.
example: There was a small crack in the windowpane.

definition: To make someone feel very unhappy; to press something down.
example: Watching too much sad news can make you feel depressed.

definition: The process of thinking about something in a logical way in order to form a conclusion or judgment.
example: Her reasoning for quitting her job was based on a desire for new challenges.

definition: (Of lines, planes, or surfaces) side by side and having the same distance continuously between them; (verb) to be similar or correspond to.
example: The road runs parallel to the river for several miles.

definition: To involve someone in an activity or conversation; to attract and keep someone's attention.
example: The teacher tried to engage the students in a discussion about the book.

definition: Unwilling and hesitant; disinclined.
example: He was reluctant to admit that he had made a mistake.

definition: "Internal" means inside something, while "External" means outside something.
example: The company faced both internal management issues and external market pressures.

definition: To chase and kill wild animals for food or sport; to search for something.
example: Historically, the fox hunt was a popular sport in England.

definition: An amount of something that is more than necessary, permitted, or desired.
example: It's important to remove any excess water from the clothes before drying them.

definition: A place for the confinement of people accused or convicted of a crime.
example: He was sent to jail for three months for the offense.

definition: Not affected by the passage of time or by changes in fashion; eternal.
example: Shakespeare's plays are considered timeless books because their themes are still relevant today.

definition: A possible sequence of events; a plan for what might happen.
example: We need to prepare for a worst-case scenario in case the plan fails.

definition: Having or showing a modest or low estimate of one's own importance; low in rank or status.
example: In my humble opinion, this proposal is the most practical solution.

definition: A set of marks used as a standard for measuring or comparing; the relative size or extent of something.
example: The project was carried out on a large scale, involving thousands of workers.

definition: The gradual development of something, especially from a simple to a more complex form.
example: The evolution of technology has greatly changed our lives.

definition: To accept or allow something that you do not like or agree with, without complaining or interfering.
example: The school tries to foster tolerance towards all students, regardless of their background.

definition: Relating to experience, real actions, or real uses rather than ideas; useful or suitable.
example: My brother is a very practical person who always finds simple solutions to problems.

definition: Stiff or unyielding; not able to bend or change easily.
example: The old machine had a frame that would appear rigid, but it actually had a little flexibility.

definition: To crush something into small pieces or powder; to rub something against a hard surface.
example: We used a machine to grind the coffee beans.

definition: A hot glowing body of ignited gas that is generated by something on fire.
example: The flame of the candle flickered in the wind.

definition: A dry substance consisting of tiny particles, usually made by grinding a solid substance.
example: Historically, gun powder was a revolutionary invention in warfare.

definition: A course or principle of action adopted or proposed by a government, party, business, or individual.
example: The new government announced its economic policy to boost the nation's growth.

definition: Behavior showing high moral standards; a quality considered morally good or desirable.
example: Patience is a great virtue to have when teaching children.

definition: To give someone the right to have or do something.
example: All employees are entitled to receive paid vacation days.

definition: To put someone in prison or in another place from which they cannot escape.
example: The activists were falsely imprisoned for protesting peacefully.

definition: A broad piece of defensive armor held by hand; (verb) to protect someone or something.
example: The thick walls helped to shield the building against the strong winds.

definition: To be brave enough to do something; to challenge someone to do something.
example: How dare you! You should not speak to your elders like that.

definition: The armed forces of a country; relating to soldiers or war.
example: The country strengthened its military forces in response to regional threats.

definition: To be greater in number or size than something else; to go beyond a limit.
example: The project budget is expected to exceed the initial estimate.

definition: The average period that a person may expect to live.
example: Advances in medicine have increased life expectancy in many countries.

definition: A punishment imposed for breaking a law, rule, or contract.
example: If you cancel the contract early, you will have to pay a penalty.

definition: A device for making an electrical connection; a piece of material used to stop a hole.
example: The investors decided to pull the plug on the failing startup company.

definition: An adhesive substance used for sticking objects or materials together.
example: Don't forget to put on glue carefully when you are making the model.

definition: A set of words that is complete in itself; (verb) to declare the punishment decided for an offender.
example: The judge decided to sentence the criminal to five years in prison.

definition: Not part of the essential nature of someone or something; coming from outside.
example: Some people are driven by extrinsic motivation, such as earning money.

definition: Belonging naturally; essential.
example: The intrinsic quality of the painting was evident in its vibrant colors and detailed brushwork.
